books.title: The Bell Below
books.author: Low Bell Chapter
lore_pages: The monastery's bell hangs lower than its chapel floor. Its tower descends into the hill instead of rising above it. The sound travels first through stone, then through air.
Novices are told that this is how doctrine should travel: through what is solid before it reaches what is empty.
When the bell sounds at dusk, every voice stops until the last vibration is gone. Silence is kept not because the sky commands it, but because the ground has spoken.

books.title: Rule of Silence
books.author: Prior Edrin
lore_pages: Do not fill every emptiness with speech. Wind can be loud and still say nothing. A faithful answer may be a hand on stone, a completed task, or a road repaired before dawn.
Pilgrims sleep without conversation on their final night here. In the morning they descend by the same path they climbed. There is no secret exit and no easier road.
The Unmoored mistake speed for freedom. We practice the opposite lesson: a journey acquires meaning by the weight it asks us to carry.

books.title: Pilgrim's Bell Note
books.author: Sera of the South Road
lore_pages: I heard the low bell from outside the walls and thought thunder had entered the mountain. The brothers laughed when I said so, then apologized because laughter is forbidden after dusk.
They asked whether I feared heights. I said no. They asked whether I feared falling. I said everyone does. 'Then you understand more than you think,' one replied.
I leave tomorrow for another Chain. The route clerk gave me only one measure and told me another pilgrim would carry the rest.

books.title: Bellkeeper's Tally
books.author: Bellkeeper's Office
lore_pages: Dawn: one long toll. Midday: two. Dusk: three. Enemy sighting: five hard strokes. Sky-machine sighting: continuous ringing until the watcher confirms direction.
Repairs this season: lower axle, two braces, rope, stair lamps. The deep chamber remains dry. No cracks observed in the foundation.
Courier instruction: never amend a missing measure from memory. Missing marks are deliberate. Senior copies alone may carry a complete road.

books.title: Seal IV — The Eight Courts
books.author: Low Bell Chapter
lore_pages: Before the High Basilica stand eight courts. Each is silent at a different hour so that one court is always listening while the others speak.
The fourth court contains a bell sunk beneath the paving in imitation of this monastery. Its sound is said to travel through the whole mountain.
A pilgrim who reaches that bell has crossed nearly the full city, but the High Seat still stands above.
